claim: Agreement among declared worldviews does not protect a decision rule when every worldview shares the same omitted state.
scope: Experiment 003A robustness gate with a generated rare-tail state that was either represented in or omitted from every declared worldview.
support: Certified-non-oracle rate was 0.070125 with the tail included.
Certified-non-oracle rate was 0.08290625 with the tail omitted.
All 96 registered cells and 96,000 cases were retained.

confidence.rationale: The direction matched preregistered H3 and is deterministic within the frozen generator.

invariance: Observed in the equal-cell positive-tail aggregate.
boundary: The magnitude is specific to the registered generator, view construction, and gate; it does not estimate real omitted-scenario prevalence.
disconfirmation: A preregistered replication under the same mechanism shows omission does not increase false certification.
A gate with explicit open-world coverage tests eliminates the difference.
action_implication: Label robustness as conditional on the represented scenario and model set, and require an explicit omitted-state challenge before pilot certification.

claim: Multiplying uncertain negative impacts by confidence can move them toward zero and thereby increase exposure to severe downside.
scope: Experiment 003A cells with positive tail probability and confidence 0.4 assigned to negative declared impacts.
support: Confidence-shrink minus declared-raw catastrophe exposure was 0.006889375.
The paired case-level bootstrap 95% interval was [0.006659375, 0.007126875].
Overall confidence shrink had lower mean regret but a higher harmful-choice rate, showing a multi-metric tradeoff.

confidence.rationale: Preregistered H4 was supported with a narrow paired interval and a direct algebraic mechanism.

invariance: Aggregated across registered visibility, probability-error, impact-error, value-shift, and positive-tail conditions.
boundary: The generator assigned lower confidence selectively to negative impacts; symmetric uncertainty sets or conservative bounds can behave differently.
disconfirmation: A faithful replication finds no increase in downside exposure.
A formal demonstration shows the scoring rule cannot favor an option by attenuating its uncertain harms.
action_implication: Do not use confidence as a direct multiplier on signed consequences; represent uncertain impacts with intervals or distributions and test downside explicitly.

claim: A robustness gate can reduce tail exposure while imposing an excessive opportunity cost through deferral to baseline.
scope: Experiment 003A positive-tail, tail-included cells comparing the registered robustness gate with confidence-shrink selection.
support: The regret increase 1.879184 exceeded the preregistered allowance 1.331028; H5 was not supported.

confidence.rationale: The registered joint criterion failed after correction of a documented result-classification bug.

invariance: All included-tail grid cells contributed equally.
boundary: Baseline quality and the relative social loss of catastrophes versus forgone gains determine whether this tradeoff is acceptable.
disconfirmation: A replication meeting the frozen joint-protection criterion shows the gate reduces one risk without excessive increase in the other.
action_implication: Evaluate abstention and safety gates on opportunity cost as well as avoided harm; never count deferral alone as success.

claim: Minimax regret does not provide downside protection merely by name; its performance depends on whether the declared uncertainty set contains the consequential errors.
scope: Experiment 003A registered alternative probability and stakeholder-weight views in included-tail cells with estimation error.
support: Minimax P90 regret was 3.648929 versus 3.643432 for declared raw.
The paired mean-regret difference was -0.001315 with bootstrap interval [-0.008142, 0.006058].

confidence.rationale: The null result is stable for the registered view set; its external scope is deliberately narrow.

invariance: Computed over all registered included-tail cells with at least one active error factor.
boundary: Richer uncertainty sets, different regret definitions, or adversarially generated views can produce benefit.
disconfirmation: A faithful replication shows lower P90 regret under the same registered view set.
action_implication: Audit the coverage and construction of an uncertainty set before treating minimax output as robust.

claim: A registered fairness or harm metric that never activates cannot support a conclusion of distributional safety.
scope: Experiment 003A affected-party expected-harm threshold of -40 under the registered impact ranges and tail probabilities.
support: Affected-party harm rate was zero for every method and value-shift condition.
Preregistered H7 was not supported because the outcome contained no variation.

confidence.rationale: The benchmark output directly establishes that this metric was dormant, not that real distributional harm is absent.

invariance: Zero across all 96 registered cells and six methods.
boundary: This is a diagnostic about the benchmark, not a substantive distributional finding.
disconfirmation: Recalculation reveals threshold crossings that were missed by the implementation.
action_implication: Redesign the next generator around stakeholder conflict and continuous inequality-sensitive losses before evaluating distributional robustness.
